established.method: Semantic revert, observed live in this session rather than reconstructed. Before databaseConnection() existed, app/lib/prisma.ts built the adapter from the connection string alone (new PrismaPg({connectionString})), which is exactly the reverted world: pg does not parse Prisma's ?schema= parameter, so the session stayed on the default search_path. prove-red cannot take this by revert — reverting app/lib/prisma.ts restores its better-sqlite3 form, which does not compile against the postgresql schema, and reverting app/lib/databaseUrl.ts deletes the symbol the test imports.
established.evidence: Measured across two full suite runs. With the connection string passed alone: 62 failed / 979 passed, every one of the 61 integration failures resolving to the same Postgres 42P01 — 'relation "public.ThinkingMap" does not exist' — captured directly from a tsx probe of setUpTestSchema, with the tables verifiably present in the test_* schema that db push had created. After lifting ?schema= out and passing it as PrismaPg's schema option, with no other change: 0 failed / 1046 passed.

attested: databaseConnection › lifts the schema out of the connection string
